memory_candidates.content: When an issues.jsonl entry's resolution field is null/omitted, treat it identically to "open" in orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's filter predicate (.resolution // "open", not .resolution // ""). The closed resolution enum (fixed_inline|worked_around|open) has no value meaning "deliberately not worth acting on" -- so merging null into open's meaning loses no expressive capability the schema already offered, it only removes a provenance distinction (explicit vs. implicit), which a lightweight implicit-open tally can recover without re-tightening the writer.

Before picking between 'tighten the writer' (require a field going forward) and 'widen the reader' (reinterpret an existing null/missing value) as a remedy for a silently-dropped-data defect, check whether the acceptance test requires fixing already-written, append-only data that cannot be retroactively edited. Tightening the writer only prevents recurrence and cannot rescue historical entries; widening the reader can do both in one change. This ruled out 'tighten the writer' as the sole remedy for the issues.jsonl null-resolution defect (task 373) because a regression fixture over already-archived tasks required the historical entries to become reachable without editing them.
